title: Analog Read Serial
description: Read a potentiometer and print its changing value to the Serial Monitor, using analogRead() and Serial.println().

steps.clip: Let's read a potentiometer! Grab your Arduino Uno, a breadboard, a 10k potentiometer, and some jumper wires.
Push the potentiometer's three legs into the breadboard, straddling three neighboring columns.
hints: All three legs go in at once — it's one part.
Make sure each leg lands in its own column so they don't touch each other.

steps.clip: Run a black wire from one of the potentiometer's outer legs to a GND pin on the Arduino.
hints: Either outer leg can be the ground side — they're interchangeable.
Black is the traditional color for ground wires.

steps.clip: Now run a red wire from the potentiometer's other outer leg to the 5V pin on the Arduino.
hints: This is the remaining outer leg — whichever one you haven't wired yet.
This powers the potentiometer so it can produce a voltage to read.

steps.clip: Finally, run a yellow wire from the potentiometer's middle leg — the wiper — to pin A0.
hints: The middle leg is the signal pin — its voltage changes as you turn the knob.
A0 is one of the analog input pins, labeled on the board near the bottom.

steps.clip: Time to upload the code! Open the Serial Monitor afterward and watch the numbers change as you turn the knob.
